passages.title: Passage 1
passages.instructions:
Questions 1–40

You should spend about 60 minutes on Questions 1–40, which are based on the reading passage below.
passages.body:
Attachment Across the Lifespan

A Attachment theory describes how early caregiver responsiveness shapes expectations about trust, comfort, and exploration across the lifespan. Infants develop internal working models that guide social behaviour in childhood friendships, adolescent romance, and adult partnerships. Longitudinal studies following cohorts for decades link secure patterns with better emotion regulation, though change remains possible after supportive therapy or stable relationships later in life. Critics caution against deterministic readings that blame parents for all adult difficulties while ignoring poverty, discrimination, and neighbourhood violence. Scholars caution that cross-national comparisons require careful attention to institutional context and data quality. Policy evaluations therefore depend on transparent reporting and independent replication of key results.

B Strange Situation experiments classify toddler behaviour toward reunions after brief separations, distinguishing secure, avoidant, ambivalent, and disorganised patterns. Cross-cultural replication shows category prevalence varies, prompting debate about universal versus culturally embedded norms of closeness. Daycare expansion led researchers to examine multiple caregivers without assuming maternal exclusivity determines outcomes. Quality of sensitivity—prompt comforting, coherent narratives—predicts security more reliably than hours apart, according to meta-analyses synthesising hundreds of observational studies from North America, Europe, and East Asia. Policy evaluations therefore depend on transparent reporting and independent replication of key results. Longitudinal studies remain essential before drawing firm conclusions about causal mechanisms and durable outcomes.

C Adolescent attachment reorganises as peers and romantic partners become salient figures while family bonds remain foundational. Secure teens explore identity with less reckless compensation, whereas insecure youth may cling or dismiss intimacy when stressed. School transitions and migration disrupt familiar networks, temporarily elevating anxiety that supportive mentors can buffer. Neuroimaging studies report associations between reported security and prefrontal regulation of amygdala responses during social rejection tasks, though correlation does not prove causal direction or immutable traits. Longitudinal studies remain essential before drawing firm conclusions about causal mechanisms and durable outcomes. Scholars caution that cross-national comparisons require careful attention to institutional context and data quality.

D Adult romantic attachment inventories measure anxiety and avoidance dimensions on continuous scales rather than categorical labels alone. Couples therapy using emotionally focused techniques aims to reshape interaction cycles that perpetuate protest or withdrawal. Workplace research explores how leaders with secure profiles foster psychological safety, while dismissive styles may trivialise subordinate concerns. The author warns against pop psychology quizzes that oversimplify complex histories into fixed types without clinical interviewing or attention to trauma overlays that mimic insecure presentations. Scholars caution that cross-national comparisons require careful attention to institutional context and data quality. Policy evaluations therefore depend on transparent reporting and independent replication of key results.

E Ageing introduces attachment needs around illness, bereavement, and relocation to care homes where staff turnover threatens continuity. Spousal loss among older adults can reactivate earlier insecurities, complicating grief with panic or numbness. Intergenerational support flows bidirectionally when adult children coordinate end-of-life care, sometimes reviving childhood dynamics in stressful decision meetings. Programmes pairing residents with consistent volunteers aim to rebuild reliable bonds, reducing agitation in dementia wards where unfamiliar faces trigger fear responses misread as behavioural problems only. Policy evaluations therefore depend on transparent reporting and independent replication of key results. Longitudinal studies remain essential before drawing firm conclusions about causal mechanisms and durable outcomes.

F Clinical interventions include parent-infant coaching, circle of security groups, and mentalisation-based therapies strengthening reflective capacity about one's own and others' minds. Foster and adoption systems prioritise placement stability because multiple disruptions correlate with disorganised profiles and educational struggles. Policy implications span paid parental leave, affordable mental health coverage, and domestic violence prevention protecting caregivers and children simultaneously. The writer contends attachment science should inform systems design, not merely individual counselling markets priced beyond reach of disadvantaged families. Longitudinal studies remain essential before drawing firm conclusions about causal mechanisms and durable outcomes. Scholars caution that cross-national comparisons require careful attention to institutional context and data quality.

G Looking ahead, integrative models will combine genetics, epigenetics, and social context without reviving simplistic nature-nurture splits. Open science practices sharing anonymised longitudinal datasets could improve reproducibility across laboratories. If popular media reduce attachment to blame narratives, the author fears stigma will deter help-seeking. Respectful translation of research into parenting support, education, and elder care policies offers a compassionate application that honours both resilience and the enduring human need for dependable connection. Scholars caution that cross-national comparisons require careful attention to institutional context and data quality. Policy evaluations therefore depend on transparent reporting and independent replication of key results.
